gate: n/a (CPU-only analysis of GPU measurement logs; no gate run)
method: measure_act_curve.py (from gpu-sim-7uz2) run on the idle RTX 5090 at two contrasting shapes, d_ff/d=4 and batch 1 held fixed so the comparison is about SHAPE not size. Logs are the script's per-rep stdout lines (seq=... rep=... af=...).
caveat: CORRECTED 2026-10-29 TWICE. First: an earlier version said neighbour occupancy was NOT recorded -- FALSE, the logs carry neighbours_before/after. Second: the replacement text then quoted wrong figures (~4.0 GB vs ~0.8 GB). Those were wrong because the 2418 MiB entry is THE MEASURING PROCESS ITSELF and because I compared one run's PRE snapshot with another's POST snapshot. Corrected from pure-neighbour snapshots: 1132 vs 916 MiB originally, 1407 vs 1113 MiB on re-measure -- a 220-290 MiB asymmetry. The spread stays non-provisional on the orthogonal basis: per-rep values are BIT-IDENTICAL across two sessions whose occupancy totals differ ~25%, which no occupancy artefact would produce.
finding: act_factor is SHAPE-DEPENDENT AT SHORT SEQUENCE and CONVERGES AT LONG SEQUENCE: 48% across shapes at seq 2048, 1.0-1.3% at seq 16384-32768. The single-curve simplification the error budget relies on is therefore VALID WHERE IT IS USED (the deciding cell N16_seq32768) and invalid at short sequences.
mechanism: At long sequence the activation term is dominated by real token activations (scaling with seq x d x layers), so the per-token-per-layer coefficient converges across shapes. At short sequence fixed overheads -- allocator behaviour, fragmentation, workspace -- dominate and are attributed to the coefficient, which is where the apparent shape dependence comes from.
status: MEASUREMENT COMPLETE; anchoring (produced facts, doc sentence, guard + plant) still open on gpu-sim-006j.
